title: Connection Lost
dateline: The city platforms, above the bay.
mood: Alone on the city platforms, Guinevere fights her way toward the one person she has been searching for.

hero.alt: On a cracked platform in a storm-gray ruined city, Guinevere fights a gray Ender with her two drones; then heeled boots walk in under a long purple robe; then, past a staff with a dark orb, the small fight shows far below.

segs.t: The figure had dropped out of sight behind the towers. The Enders had risen to fill the gap.
Guinevere landed on a cracked stone platform, her back to a pillar. Her two cat-eared drones snapped up at her shoulders, yellow eyes burning. At her collar the star was still flashing.
They’re dangling her at me,
she thought.
Fine. I’ll bite.

She went in fists first. Elbow in, hip first, the way Hester had drilled her in the House’s yard at dawn. The drones took whatever her hands left. Gray Enders went down in heaps. Below the platform, half the district was rubble, and smoke stood up from it in columns.
She counted without meaning to.
Nine. Ten.
“Eleven,” she said aloud.
Nobody beside her said,
Then be faster.

A woman came out along the upper platform, above Guinevere’s. She wore heeled boots, white stockings and a long robe. Her staff ended in an orb as dark as a hole in the world. She moved slowly, as if she owned the place.
The Enders ran along beside her. Not one of them touched her.
From down here Guinevere could not make out a face. She did not need one. Only one person in the world could make that star beep.
Vexana.
She started forward, the name already in her mouth.
They aren’t even holding on to you. Come on. Run.
Something hummed above her.
She knew that hum. For a whole year it had come over her shoulder in every fight and hit whatever reached for her back. She had never once had to turn and check.
There you are,
she thought, and looked up.
A huge arrow of violet light was falling out of the storm, straight down at her. There was no time to dodge. It struck and burst.
When the glare cleared, she was still on her feet, her ears ringing. Her drones wheeled back to her shoulders.
The woman had stopped at the rail above, the staff lowered from the shot. Around its cracked grip ran a band of brass.
Guinevere had watched that collar go on. At the team test, Vexana had knelt behind her with a little screwdriver and fitted it, while Guinevere held the front alone.
“No...” said Guinevere.
Nobody’s holding her,
she thought.
She did that herself.
The rain came down between them. Up at the rail, nobody moved.
The star on her collar went on flashing, bright and pleased.
The haze had thinned. Blue-lavender hair, fading to magenta at the ends. Violet eyes. A small mole beside the mouth.
The hair’s wrong,
Guinevere thought. Everything else was right.
She had said it at the long table and in the counseling room.
She’s alive.
She had never pictured this.

media.alt: A blast fades into gray smoke, and as it clears Guinevere is still on her feet, her drones with her, staring up; above her a woman with pale lavender hair and violet eyes holds a staff whose orb is dark as a hole, purple stars turning around her.

segs.t: The staff came up. Violet shots cracked down at her. She dodged twice and ran for the steps, hands open, toward her.
“It can’t be,” she said.
Enders gathered at the rail behind the woman. Then they poured down the steps at Guinevere.
She planted her feet. “You would never betray us.”
She threw out both arms.
“Light of the stars, tear through the darkness.”

Light burst out of her, gold and white. It swept the platform from end to end, and every Ender in reach went down. When it faded, the way up lay open. No Enders on the steps. Nobody at the top of them but Vexana.
Vexana looked down at her. Her face did not move.
“You haven’t changed at all.”
The voice was low and flat. Every night, late, that voice had come down the phone to tell her
Go to bed.

media.alt: Close on Vexana's face: pale lavender hair with a violet streak, violet eyes, a small mole beside her mouth, no expression at all.

segs.t: Guinevere started up the steps. A great spell had been gathering in the staff the whole time she ran. Vexana let it go.
It hit her like a wall. It threw her off the platform and far down onto a lower one. She skidded across the stone and stopped against a broken rail.
On her arm guard a tiny keychain rocked on its clip: a little black-haired Vexana. She had clipped it there at the end of the first week Vexana was gone, where her fist would swing.
She counted three for herself and got up anyway.
She tipped her head back toward the platform above.
“Have you really forgotten everything, Vexana!”
Her voice cracked on the name. She made it carry.
“We made a promise to protect this world.”
The memories came as she said it, one on top of the other.

The hall under the five great stars. Colored light from the tall window lay across the rows of chairs. At the front, Lesley was giving her speech about trust to Layla, Fanny, Ruby and Angela in their combat suits.

By the door Vexana waited in her school uniform, arms folded. Guinevere stood along the wall in her own uniform. On the speech’s last words she waved at Vexana with her whole arm. At each girl’s belt hung a tiny keychain doll of the other. When the hall emptied, she took a fistful of Vexana’s sleeve and towed her out of the door into the light.

Up on the high platform, Vexana had turned her back on her, toward her Enders. Now her head came around over her shoulder, and held there. The staff dipped. Even from this far below, Guinevere could see Vexana looked lost.
She heard that,
Guinevere thought.
She’s listening. Keep going.
A city roof under a clear blue sky. Green guardrails, warm from the sun. Two small gold stars in her palm, band-aids on her fingertips, one seam a hair crooked.
“Here! I made ’em myself, ya know!”
She held the phone out at arm’s length. Vexana’s face beside hers in the little screen. A gold star glowing at each collar.
“Look, they light up when our powers are in sync.”

media.alt: Memories: in the Academy hall under tall colored windows, black-haired Vexana waits by the door while Guinevere waves her whole arm; on a sunny city roof the two stand close with gold stars; then they take a selfie together above the city.

segs.t: She had said it on that roof: “We protect this world. The two of us.” And Vexana had said, “A promise.”
She gripped the broken rail. “You were always there to pick me up,” she called up.

A claw raked her right arm, on a street at the dome’s foot that she had taken alone. Her left hand pressed over the wound, and the ground tipped up to meet her. When she opened her eyes, a black-haired girl stood over her, holding out a hand.
“Stay with me, Guinevere.”

media.alt: A memory: black-haired Vexana in her school uniform, staff in one hand, holds out her other hand on a smoky battlefield.

segs.t: Then back to back, the first time, and the street holding. The violet arrow coming down over her shoulder, the way it had every time after. Until today.
“The one I could always count on,” she shouted.
“Enough!”
Vexana’s scream rang off the stone. She came down to the lower platform, and the Enders filled in behind her. Now they stood face to face, Guinevere alone, Vexana with an army at her back.

media.alt: On a wide ruined platform under a storm sky, Vexana stands with a mass of Enders at her back, facing Guinevere, who stands alone.

segs.t: At Vexana’s right wrist, something small glowed gold through the cloth of her sleeve. A star, lit.
Guinevere’s hand closed on her own star. It was blazing, hot against her palm.
In sync,
she thought.
It only lights like this when we’re in sync. You’re in there. You’re still in there.
Vexana’s arm pressed tight against her side. The gold still showed through the cloth.
Her eyes had gone to Guinevere’s collar. Her mouth opened a little, and nothing came out.
“Why, Vexana...” said Guinevere. “Your emblem is still...”
She did not finish. The sky went dark.
Over the bay the Singularity was tearing wider. Its ragged mouth stretched into a star, and one point of it reached across the sky until it hung low over the platforms, much nearer than before.
The wind turned. Vexana’s robe whipped toward the tear, and the smoke streamed up into the open star.
